title: About Me
text:
Academic Interests
I am a Statistics student at the University of Campinas (UNICAMP), interested in understanding how statistical methods can be used to extract information from data and support quantitative reasoning.
My academic training combines statistical theory, mathematical foundations, and practical data analysis. Through coursework and independent projects, I have been developing skills in statistical programming, data visualization, modeling, and statistical inference.
My main interests include:

title: About Me
text:
Statistical inference
Sampling and survey methodology
Regression and statistical modeling
Experimental design
Exploratory and descriptive data analysis
Data visualization

title: About Me
text:
Working with Data
I am particularly interested in the process of moving from raw data to meaningful statistical conclusions: understanding the structure of a dataset, selecting appropriate methods, evaluating assumptions, and communicating results clearly.
This portfolio serves as a record of that development, bringing together projects completed during my academic training and documenting the methods used in each analysis.

title: Projects
text:
Semmelweis Handwashing Study
This section presents selected statistical projects developed throughout my academic training.
Each project focuses on a specific dataset, statistical question, or methodological problem, combining statistical reasoning with reproducible data analysis.
Statistical analysis of handwashing and maternal mortality
This project analyzes historical data from the Vienna General Hospital between 1841 and 1846 to investigate the relationship between handwashing practices and maternal mortality.
The analysis includes:
Tools: R · tidyverse · ggplot2 · Quarto
